subject: English
passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The Arctic fox (vulpes lagopus) is a small mammal that survives harsh winters by maintaining its body temperature despite extreme cold.
• It is unusual among Arctic animals in that it doesn't migrate to warmer regions during winter.
• One way it stays warm is by growing an extremely thick winter coat that provides insulation.
• Another way it stays warm is by reducing blood flow to its extremities to conserve core body heat.
• This behavior is known as peripheral vasoconstriction.
prompt: The student wants to emphasize a similarity between the two ways an Arctic fox stays warm. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: An Arctic fox never migrates to warmer regions, instead growing an extremely thick winter coat for insulation.
choices.B: Of the Arctic fox's two ways of staying warm, only one is known as peripheral vasoconstriction.
choices.C: In addition to growing a thick winter coat for insulation, an Arctic fox reduces blood flow to its extremities to conserve body heat.
choices.D: Neither of an Arctic fox's two ways of staying warm requires the animal to migrate to warmer regions.

explanation:
Choice D is the best answer. The sentence emphasizes a similarity between the two ways an Arctic fox stays warm, noting that neither way requires the animal to migrate to warmer regions.

Why B is incorrect:

Choice B is incorrect. The sentence notes the term used to describe one of the two ways that Arctic foxes stay warm; it doesn't emphasize a similarity between the two ways.
